name: AppShell
purpose: The top-level page shell — composes a SideNav, a TopBar, and the scrollable main content into one consistent full-height layout. Never write `display: flex; min-height: 100vh` by hand again.
neverUseFor: A single content section inside an already-shelled page — AppShell is used once, at the page root
Auth/marketing pages with no persistent nav — a page with no SideNav should just render its content directly, not force an empty shell
rationale: AppShell exists so no page hand-writes `display: flex; min-height: 100vh` again: it fixes one composition of SideNav, TopBar and a single scrollable <main>, which guarantees exactly one main landmark per page (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks) and a consistent scroll container across every product screen.

mayExtendLocally: Choose which SideNav entries and TopBar actions a product renders
Compose any page content inside the main slot
Omit the shell entirely on auth/marketing pages with no persistent nav
mustEscalateToDS: Adding new shell regions (e.g. a right rail or a footer bar)
Changing which element scrolls or rendering more than one <main>
Nesting AppShell inside another layout or page

anatomy.description: Flex column beside the sidenav — wraps the topbar and main.

props.name: sidenav
props.description: A SideNav instance, rendered to the left.

props.name: topbar
props.description: A TopBar instance, rendered above the main content.

a11y.role: main (implicit from <main> on app-shell-main — exactly one per page)

figma.structure: No variants or props of its own — app-shell-root (fill/page) > SideNav instance + app-shell-content (TopBar instance + app-shell-main, 24px padding = spacing/l). Main holds sample content (PageHeader + Card instances).
